entities.summary:
Curt Bräuer (1889–1969) was a German diplomat best known as envoy to Norway at the time of the April 1940 German invasion. He delivered ultimata and managed the awkward theatre of presenting aggression as political necessity while King Haakon VII and the Norwegian government refused Quisling’s coup and chose resistance and exile.

Bräuer’s mission sits at the hinge of diplomacy and Wehrmacht occupation: the Foreign Office’s attempt to cloak Operation Weserübung in negotiation collapsed within hours. Subsequent occupation politics sidelined such envoys as military and SS structures took control.

In Norwegian and diplomatic history he is a face of the failed German effort to secure quick political surrender in Oslo—an emblem of diplomacy subordinated to blitzkrieg.
